blocks.prompt: 9. A particle is projected vertically upwards with a velocity 100 m/s, and another is let fall from a height of 200 m at the same time. Find the height of the point where they meet each other.
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein do particles ek hi vertical line par chal rahe hain: ek neeche zameen se upar phenka gaya hai aur doosra 200 m ki oonchai se chhora gaya hai.
Diya kya hai? Pehle ki \(u = 100\) m/s upar ki taraf; doosre ki \(u = 0\), oonchai 200 m; dono ek hi waqt par shuru.
Find kya karna hai? Woh oonchai jahan dono milte hain.
Rule kaunsa? Dono par sirf gravity lag rahi hai, is liye dono ke liye \(x = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2\) chalega.
Plan: har particle ki oonchai ko \(t\) ke formula mein likhein, dono ko barabar karein, \(t\) nikalein, phir oonchai.
steps:
Diya gaya: pehla particle zameen se \(u = 100\) m/s upar; doosra particle us ke theek upar 200 m ki oonchai se \(u = 0\) (sirf chhora gaya); dono ek saath shuru; \(g = 9.8\ \text{m/s}^2\).
Maloom karna: milne wali jagah ki oonchai.
Tareeqa: Oonchai zameen se upar ki taraf naapenge. Har particle ke liye \(x = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2\) lagayenge; kitab ke rule ke mutabiq upar jane wali motion mein \(a = -g\) aur neeche aane wali mein \(a = g\). Milne ka matlab hai dono ki oonchai ek hi waqt par barabar ho.

Pehle particle ki oonchai
\[h_1 = 100t + \dfrac{1}{2}(-9.8)t^2\]
\[h_1 = 100t - 4.9t^2 \quad (1)\]
Kyun: Humne upar ki direction ko positive liya hai, aur gravity neeche kheenchti hai, is liye is particle ke liye \(a = -g = -9.8\). Yani har second is ki speed 9.8 m/s kam hoti jati hai.

Doosre particle ki oonchai
\[\text{fall} = 0 + \dfrac{1}{2}(9.8)t^2 = 4.9t^2\]
\[h_2 = 200 - 4.9t^2 \quad (2)\]
Kyun: Yeh rest se girta hai, is liye \(u = 0\) aur \(a = g\). \(t\) second mein yeh \(4.9t^2\) neeche aata hai, to zameen se is ki oonchai 200 mein se itna minus hogi.
Dhyan dein: \(4.9t^2\) gira hua distance hai, oonchai nahi; oonchai ke liye 200 se minus karna zaroori hai.

Milne ki shart: dono oonchaiyan barabar
\[100t - 4.9t^2 = 200 - 4.9t^2\]
\[100t = 200\]
\[t = 2\ \text{s}\]
Kyun: Milne ka matlab hai ek hi waqt par ek hi jagah hona, is liye \(h_1 = h_2\) rakha. Dono taraf \(-4.9t^2\) hai, woh cancel ho gaya, kyunke dono par gravity ka asar bilkul barabar hai.

Milne wali jagah ki oonchai
\[h_1 = 100(2) - 4.9(2)^2\]
\[= 200 - 19.6 = 180.4\ \text{m}\]
Kyun: \(t = 2\) ko equation (1) mein rakh diya. Yeh zameen se oonchai hai. Sawal milne ka waqt nahi, milne ki jagah ki oonchai poochta hai, is liye \(t\) nikal kar ruk jana kaafi nahi.
Dhyan dein: \(4.9(2)^2\) mein pehle square karein (4), phir 4.9 se multiply karein; \(9.8^2\) jaisi ghalti na karein.

Tasdeeq
\[h_2 = 200 - 4.9(4) = 180.4\ \text{m}\ \checkmark\]
\[v_1 = 100 - 9.8(2) = 80.4\ \text{m/s}\]
Kyun: Equation (2) se bhi wohi oonchai aayi. Pehle particle ki velocity abhi bhi positive hai, yani woh abhi upar ja raha hai jab dono milte hain; doosra sirf 19.6 m gira hai. Sab kuch hawa mein hi ho raha hai, jawab mantiqi hai.
blocks.final_answer: Dono zameen se \(180.4\) m ki oonchai par, shuru hone ke \(2\) s baad milte hain.

answer_figure.alt: Height-time graph: the rising curve h = 100t - 4.9t^2 from the origin and the falling curve h = 200 - 4.9t^2 from 200 meet at the point (2, 180.4).
answer_figure.caption: Heights of the two particles; they meet at t = 2 s, 180.4 m above the ground (original drawing)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Kitab Exercise 7.1 ka koi answer print nahi karti, is liye yeh jawab hamara apna hai. Humne isay computer algebra (sympy) se aur ek alag hal kiye gaye solution se alag alag check kiya hai, is liye aap is par bharosa kar sakte hain. Phir bhi apna jawab khud check karne ki aadat zaroor daliye. Hum yeh maan rahe hain (jaisa sawal ka maqsad hai) ke pehla particle zameen se, doosre ke theek neeche se phenka gaya. Shortcut: dono ka acceleration ek jaisa hai, is liye un ke darmiyan 200 m ka faasla 100 m/s ki barabar raftaar se kam hota hai, aur \(t = 200/100 = 2\) s foran mil jata hai.
